subject: Committed usage wallet and ramp schedule — structure questions

From: Lisa Wong <lisa.wong@greenleaf.ai>

Subject: Committed spend drawdown structure — initial questions

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo last week — Greenleaf is seriously considering a committed model but our finance team has a few specific questions about how Redwood’s prepay wallet and drawdown mechanics work for multi-year deals. Can you confirm the following?

- If we do a 3-year committed prepay, how does the wallet actually burn down? Is it purely usage-driven (per-token), or do you support scheduled drawdown (e.g., monthly/quarterly amortization targets)?
- What happens to unused prepay at the end of a year vs. the end of the term? Any expiry or refund rules we should expect?
- Can we structure ramp schedules (year 1 ramp to target, year 2 steady-state)? Any discount changes if usage is below ramp targets?
- How are top-ups handled mid-term (automatic top-up triggers vs. manual)? Any minimum top-up increments?
- We need exportable consumption reporting for our GL team on a monthly cadence; is there a standard output (CSV/GL mapping)?
- Any special invoicing/recognition options (monthly amortization of prepaid vs. immediate revenue recognition)?

Attached is our procurement checklist to help pinpoint additional compliance items. Would like to sync early next week — can you send a short options memo we can share with finance?

Best,
Lisa Wong
Head of Procurement
Greenleaf AI

Hi Lisa — thanks, and great questions. I summarized three pragmatic structures we commonly offer and highlighted trade-offs for finance and procurement. Short version and attached term sheet (stub).

Option A — Annual Prepay (reset each 12 months)
- You prepay for 12 months at the start of each year; usage draws down the wallet by actual consumption.
- Unused credits expire at year-end unless you roll them into a paid top-up; refunds are possible by exception with a pro-rated admin fee.
- Discount: single-year prepay tier (e.g., ~15% off list).
- Accounting: finance can amortize monthly against consumption; Redwood provides monthly export.

Option B — Multi-year Prepay with Scheduled Drawdown (recommended for multi-year commits)
- Lump-sum prepay with a multi-year term (2–3 years). Wallet balance burns by usage, but contract includes scheduled drawdown targets (quarterly or monthly) to align usage forecasts and discount eligibility.
- If usage is below ramp targets, we include a make-good/rebilling mechanism or step-down discount protection.
- Discount: deeper than single-year (example 22% for 2yr, 28% for 3yr, exacts depend on split and payment timing).
- Accounting: supports either immediate recognition with monthly refunds/true-ups or contract amortization per customer policy; we supply GL-ready exports and a monthly burn report.

Option C — Usage-based Commit with Rolling Wallet (flexible, usage-first)
- Commit to a USD/year consumption target with monthly true-ups. Prepay wallet seeded at start, auto-top-ups triggered when balance hits threshold.
- Overage handled at negotiated overage rates or drawn from a separate monthly invoice bucket.
- Discount: tiered against committed annual volume; flexible ramp allowed within agreed thresholds.

Attachments: Redwood_CUW_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf (term sheet stub with sample ramp/discount table).

Quick ask: can you share a 12/24/36 month expected consumption curve (monthly or quarterly granularity)? That lets us map discount tiers and recommend specific ramp splits. Happy to do a 30–45 minute alignment call early next week — propose Tue/Wed.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Folks — forwarding Greenleaf’s procurement checklist and their questions above. Quick internal position before we propose anything final:

- Customer signal: evaluating for platform-wide usage — likely a multi-year commit but will want ramp flexibility (year 1 ~30–40% of target).
- Pricing flexibility: we can go up to 28% on a 3-year prepaid with staged payouts, but finance will want to push for amortization-friendly terms (i.e., monthly reporting + true-ups).
- Proposal idea: two options for the commercials — (1) 2-year, 60/40 split paid upfront with 22% discount; (2) 3-year, 40/30/30 split with 28% discount and quarterly true-ups. Include an auto-top-up trigger at 10% balance remaining.

Risks / internal asks:
- Finance: need clear guidance on revenue recognition and a refund window if they terminate within 12 months (we can cap admin refund to unused balance minus 10% admin).
- Legal: alignment on make-good mechanics if they miss ramp targets — suggest a soft step-down (discount reduction) with a 30-day cure period.

Will draft a succinct commercial note for Lisa with the two options and a sample amortization/GL export. Any redlines or better ideas?

Thanks,
Sean

Thanks, Sean — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from our finance/procurement side:

- Refunds/expiry: Greenleaf’s policy prefers a 12-month refundable window on unused prepay in case of material under-utilization; would Redwood accept a limited refund (pro-rated) if spend is below 70% of committed annual target? If not, we need clear roll-forward rules.
- Top-ups: We prefer an automatic top-up with a notification + 3-day approval window; minimum top-up $50k.
- Ramp protection: Can you include an explicit ramp schedule in the SOW so our auditors have something to map against?
- Reporting: monthly CSV export with fields (date, API key, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_center).

Lisa — appreciate the clarity. Based on your asks we’ll propose the following in the commercial note and SOW draft ahead of the call:

Proposed commercial structure (summary)
- Product: Committed Usage Wallet (CUW) with optional multi-year prepay.
- Payment & splits: 3-year example: total committed USD 1,500,000 with a 40/30/30 payment schedule (Year1/Year2/Year3). Year1 seeded wallet at signature.
- Discount tiers (examples): 1yr prepay = 15% off list; 2yr = 22%; 3yr = 28% (finals subject to consumption curve).
- Ramp schedule & Make-good: Year1 target = 35% of committed annualized usage; if actual < 70% of target for two consecutive quarters, discount steps down by 5% after a 30-day cure period (remedied via additional top-up or agreed true-up).
- Refunds/expiry: Unused wallet balances are refundable within 12 months from payment date, pro-rated minus a 10% administrative fee; refunds require 45 days advance notice.
- Top-ups: Auto-top-up trigger at 10% remaining balance; auto-top-up executed after customer approval within a 3-business-day window; minimum top-up $50,000.
- Reporting & accounting: Monthly CSV export (tokens_in/out, model, cost_center); optional GL mapping file for finance. We’ll include a sample amortization schedule in the SOW showing monthly recognition vs. remaining wallet.

Attachments for the call: Redwood_CUW_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf (commercial), sample monthly burn CSV template, and a draft SOW outline. I’ll also include a DocuSign preview link for the term sheet so your legal can quickly see the clauses.

Next steps:
- I’ll send the commercial note + SOW draft by EOD today.
- Proposed meeting Thu 11/14 11:00 AM PT with FP&A + Legal. Please confirm attendees.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the line.
